text.p: Although world population growth rates have slowed, growing numbers of women are reaching childbearing age in developing countries, according to a study released on Sunday by a population research and advocacy group.

Population Action International said global population is growing by about 1.5 percent a year, but the number of women aged 15-49 is growing in developing nations by 2.3 percent, or 24 million people.
Spending on family planning will have to increase just to keep services available to the same proportion of women who now have it, 54 percent, the group said.

The organisation said that although average family size is falling, aproximately 120 million women who do not want to become pregnant again do not have adequate access to safe and effective contraception.
The organisation urged the U.S. Congress to soften last year's budget cuts for international family planning.
The group said stabilising population is important for fighting poverty, controlling urbanization, and ensuring that there are enough basic resources like drinkable water.

"The cumulative evidence is strong that current rates of population growth pose significant and interacting risks to human well-being -- risks Americans need to be aware of," said Robert Engelman, author of the group's new study and resource book.
